speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether the Government has a standard protocol of consulting the authorities of the intended receiving countries before proceeding with the deportations of foreigners convicted of offences in Singapore; and (b) in the case of a money laundering convict who was deported from Singapore to Cambodia in June 2024 and subsequently expelled by Cambodia after one month, what consultations did the Government undertake with the Cambodian authorities before deporting him there.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: [Please refer to "Factors Considered in Deciding Deportation Destinations for Foreigners Who Have Served Their Sentences in Singapore", Official Report, 2 July 2024, Vol 95, Issue 137, Oral Answers to Questions section.] The foreign country can, as a sovereign state, choose to allow entry or it can choose to disallow entry when the person arrives on its shores, or it can take subsequent actions to expel the person after entry.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Discussions may sometimes take place for operational security reasons, for intelligence reasons, other similar purposes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Deputy Speaker, I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, I accept that there could be some operational considerations and not revealing too much information.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to say that upfront.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, my question is, is the Ministry concerned that the offender would tend to choose a jurisdiction which he considers to be favourable to him?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: By that, I mean that he might be concerned about possible prosecution for the predicate offences which led to the money laundering, for instance.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Would that be something that the Government would take into account, that he may choose a jurisdiction that would actually facilitate his avoiding prosecution for certain other crimes that he may have committed overseas?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That is the first question: whether the Government is concerned about this in giving the offender the choice.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They can choose to go to where they want to go.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Second, as regards the choice of deportation and whether that is part of the plea bargain process, again, strictly speaking, if the offender, the person who is asked to leave, can choose to go wherever he wishes to go to, then the relevance of it becomes small.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is a matter between the Attorney-General's Chambers and the defendant's lawyers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I cannot rule out that these discussions take place, but I can tell you what the legal position is.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier, the Minister mentioned that what might happen in the jurisdiction that is chosen is legally irrelevant.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I am just wondering whether he will agree with me that money laundering, being transnational in nature, that we would also like to be seen to be doing our part to ensure that the offenders face justice for whatever offences they have committed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, as such, are we not interested in the likelihood of such offenders facing prosecution or being charged for any predicate offences that they may have committed overseas and to that extent, we should play our part as well?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Well, in the first place, they would have served time in Singapore if they have committed an offence here.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But it is wishful thinking to think that every other country will take the same approach or that we can control how other countries can or cannot operationalise their legal position.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the Member were to ask any country, they will all tell the Member that they take it very seriously.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There has got to be a multiple set of considerations.
